subject: Service provider classification and US privacy addendum — transfer mechanism options
messages:
From: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@nimbushealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@nimbushealth.com
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood — CCPA/CPRA addendum + cross-border transfers

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this — quick background: Nimbus is evaluating Redwood for our patient-facing ingestion pipeline. Our legal/procurement team has a couple of privacy questions before we can move to a PO. Two main points:

1) Classification under CCPA/CPRA: we expect vendors to sign an addendum confirming service provider/processor status (i.e., not a controller, no sale of personal info). We need confirmation Redwood will accept typical "Service Provider" language or an equivalent rider we can attach.

2) Cross-border transfers: some of our customer data will move to processing services in the US. Can you confirm typical transfer mechanisms Redwood offers (SCCs, reliance on US service provider carve-outs, or any BCRs)? If SCCs, do you provide the signed annex or do you expect the customer-side to paste in the standard language? Also: any restrictions on telemetry/analytics that would require additional contractual language?

If you can send an annotated DPA or draft addendum and a simple dataflow mapping showing subprocessors (especially telemetry/metrics vendors), that would be very helpful. We are hoping to finalize terms before our next sprint review on Aug 28.

Appreciate it — Evan

--
Evan Shaw
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Health
evanshaw@NimbusHealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0199
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood — CCPA/CPRA addendum + cross-border transfers

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear summary. High-level answers below and I attached an annotated DPA and a short dataflow matrix (stubs) for subprocessors.

- Service provider designation: Redwood accepts "Service Provider" / processor language for US state privacy addenda (we do not seek controller status for customer data we process on behalf of customers). We will sign the Nimbus Health US privacy addendum with the standard "Service Provider" wording you referenced.

- Sale of personal information: Redwood does not "sell" personal information as defined under CCPA/CPRA. We will agree to contractual language that disavows any sale for customer data processed under a customer contract.

- Cross-border transfer approach: Redwood is headquartered in the US. For transfers out of the EEA/UK (if that becomes relevant) we typically provide standard SCCs and a signed addendum; for US customers transferring into US-hosted services the typical path is:
  * We process in the US by default; if you require EU/UK residency we offer Private deployment options (VPC/region lock).
  * For customers who need SCCs we can provide the standard SCC annex for the relevant jurisdiction and execute as part of the DPA.
  * We do not rely on BCRs.

- Subprocessors / telemetry: the attached matrix lists persistent subprocessors (metrics ingestion, crash reporting, cloud infra). Telemetry is limited to anonymized performance metrics unless otherwise agreed in the contract; if Nimbus requires telemetry to be disabled or more restrictive controls, we can capture that in the addendum.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I attached an annotated Redwood_DPA_v3_annotated.pdf with comments where Nimbus might want small edits.
2) If you prefer, send your US privacy addendum and we can redline it.
3) If you need an executed SCC annex, flag that and we'll include it in the DocuSign packet.

I copied the compliance and sales leads internally for any commercial or operational questions (looped separately). Happy to jump on a 30m call if helpful.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
--
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_annotated.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB), redwood-dataflow-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)

Hi Marissa / Lauren — FYI and request for quick input. Below is the inbound from Nimbus (procurement). I sent the short answers above and attached our annotated DPA + dataflow matrix. Points I want confirmation on:

- Marissa: confirm the subprocessors list is accurate for telemetry & analytics; Nimbus asked whether we can restrict telemetry by contract (they may require opt-out). Is disabling telemetry across a managed-hosted customer feasible without engineering churn?

- Lauren: they asked whether we provide the SCC annex signed or expect the customer to paste it in. Typically we include the SCCs in our DPA package and sign on our side; confirm we can include the annex and that commercial will be fine with including DocuSign flow for SCC as part of the PO. Also: if they opt for a Private deployment for residency we'd need procurement lead time — roughly estimate?

I flagged the key contractual points in the PDF (see comments). Seeking quick yes/nos so I can push back or accept small edits.

Thanks — Stephanie

From: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@nimbushealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2025 12:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood — CCPA/CPRA addendum + cross-border transfers

Stephanie — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups from our legal team after review of your annotated DPA:

1) Subprocessors: we see three telemetry/metrics subprocessors listed. Can you confirm whether any of those subprocessors receive plain-text PHI (we process limited PHI in transit for some flows)? If so, we'll need more granular controls. If not, a contractual statement that subprocessors will not process PHI in plain text (and that encryption-in-transit is enforced) should be fine.

2) SCCs: we would appreciate Redwood including the SCC annex in the DocuSign packet and signing on Redwood's side; please also include the customer-side placeholders so we can sign in the same flow.

3) Telemetry opt-out: Nimbus would prefer a contractual option to opt-out of telemetry collection for any customer-controlled environment (hosted or private). Is that something Redwood can accept as a clause in the US privacy addendum? If engineering needs time, a temporary commercial credit for disabled telemetry could be a stop-gap.

If you can send a DocuSign link with the DPA + SCC annex + the addendum redline (we attached our internal addendum earlier), we can route for signature this week.

Thanks — Evan

--
Evan Shaw
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Health
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@nimbushealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2025 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood — CCPA/CPRA addendum + cross-border transfers

Evan — quick reply to close the loop:

- Subprocessors & PHI: Marissa confirms none of the telemetry subprocessors persistently store plaintext PHI. All telemetry is collected over TLS and we require encryption-at-rest for any storage. We'll add a clause that subprocessors will not process plaintext PHI and the standard encryption-in-transit requirement to the addendum.

- SCCs: we will include the SCC annex in the DocuSign packet and sign on Redwood's side. I'll ask ops to prepare the DocuSign bundle (DPA + SCC annex + your addendum redline).

- Telemetry opt-out: Product/Engineering flagged that a telemetry opt-out for managed hosted customers is feasible as a configurational switch but requires a short lead (1–2 weeks) for Ops to apply per-customer flags; for Private deployments it is straightforward. Commercial can offer a temporary credit if you prefer immediate opt-out while we flip the config.

I'll have the DocuSign link and the final redline over by EOD. Thanks for the clear asks — this should be straightforward.

Best,
Stephanie

--
